Horodok Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record contains a discrepancy worth noting: local historians say this cemetery was closed by the Austrian government in the 1770s, when a New cemetery opened nearby — yet it is also marked on an Austro-Hungarian map from the 1860s, decades after that claimed closure. Horodok — known in Yiddish as Greiding — had a Jewish community from 1445 that grew to 3,866 by 1910, predominantly following Belz Hasidism, documented elsewhere in this collection. This cemetery was destroyed during WWII, its tombstones used for road construction; a 2012 Lo Tishkach expedition found its old brick fencing partly preserved.
